title: Approve amateur traffic and security scope
description:
Obtain human approval or rejection of the complete experimental traffic/security policy and bounded coding scope. Inventory application, control, forwarding, custody, gateway and security-establishment traffic. Review callsign/control choices and the 97.113(a)(4)/97.311 implications of confidentiality versus readable authenticated traffic.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Keep production authentication and audited OSCORE/EDHOC internals unchanged absent their separate human-only approval. An attached research proposal or closed gate is not consent. Denial or unresolved scope blocks/defer dependent implementation and RF; authority.10 is still required per actual session.
acceptance_criteria: Record allowed, forbidden and unresolved traffic with evidence; a no-go or unresolved review is valid and does not authorize implementation or operation. For positive profile/security/coding approval: Require recorded, scoped, explicit approval from Mark for the named action. Ordinary OSCORE is not presumed amateur-permitted, nor may it be automatically disabled. No public-key publication or forwarding assumption is accepted as a confidentiality exemption.
